title: Regex highlighter
description: Type an extended regular expression and watch it light up in a TuxPixel build log, with the `grep -E` command and the lines it would print.
intro: Start with the preset `sl.me` and see which lines light up. Then change the dot to `[iy]` and predict whether the result changes before you look. Try `ghosts?`, then `files$`, and finally `o*`: ask yourself why every line matches that one.
takeaways: In `grep -E` (extended regular expressions) a dot matches any one character, `[abc]` matches one character from the set, `*` repeats the item before it zero or more times, `+` one or more times and `?` makes it optional.
`^` anchors a pattern to the start of the line and `$` to the end, so `files$` finds only lines that end in `files`. To match a literal dot, write `\.`.

`|` means or: `ERROR|WARN` prints the lines that contain either word. Without `-E`, plain `grep` reads `|`, `+`, `?` and `(` as ordinary characters, and you would need a backslash in front to give them their special meaning.
A pattern with `*` can match zero characters, so `o*` matches every line. A line is printed when the pattern matches anywhere in it, not only when it matches the whole line.

When a pattern could match more than one stretch of text, `grep` highlights the leftmost match and, from there, the longest one. Quote the pattern in single quotes so the shell does not treat `*`, `?`, `|` and `$` as its own symbols.

log: 09:00:09 WARN  goblin.png is 3 pixels too wide
09:00:20 WARN  boss-theme.ogg is 2.1 MB, limit is 2 MB
09:00:35 INFO  tested bat, ghost and ghosts: all spawn
09:00:40 INFO  build finished in 39 s with 3 errors

presets.title: A plain word
presets.explain: Letters match themselves, so this prints the three lines that contain `ERROR`.

presets.title: Either word
presets.explain: `|` means or. It needs `grep -E`; plain `grep` would look for a literal bar.

presets.title: Any one character
presets.explain: The dot stands for exactly one character, so `slime` and `slyme` both match, but `slme` would not.

presets.title: One of a set
presets.explain: `[iy]` matches one character, `i` or `y`. It is stricter than a dot: `slume` would not match.

presets.title: Optional character
presets.explain: `?` makes the `s` optional, so the line matches whether it says `ghost` or `ghosts`. Highlighting shows the longer match.

presets.title: One or more digits
presets.explain: `[0-9]` is one digit and `+` asks for one or more of them, so `128 files` and `7 files` match.

presets.title: End of line
presets.explain: `$` anchors the pattern to the end of the line. `files` elsewhere in a line would not count.

presets.title: Start of line
presets.explain: `^` anchors the pattern to the start of the line. Here it also fixes the seconds to 00 to 29 and requires `ERROR` right after the time.

presets.title: A literal dot
presets.explain: A backslash takes the special meaning away, so `\.` is a real dot. Plain `1.4.2` would also match `1x4y2`.

presets.title: Dot and star together
presets.explain: `.*` means any number of any characters. It matches as much as it can, so the highlight runs to the last `e` on the line.

presets.title: The zero trap
presets.explain: `o*` is allowed to match zero letters, so it matches every line. Only lines with an `o` get a highlight.
